C-STREAM-BUDGET.Name: Per-session stream budgets (bytes, sections, rate) — implementation plan
C-STREAM-BUDGET.IntentSummary: Enforce per-session resource budgets on the M-045 streaming document session against the post-#298 structures in the beta-gate-wave worktree: handle_doc_open (src-tauri/src/m045_ext/live_server.rs:745), handle_doc_patch (live_server.rs:861), with HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SECS (live_server.rs:1467) the only existing cap. Three budget classes, all pinned as named constants: STREAM_BUDGET_TOTAL_BYTES = 67108864 (64 MiB cumulative accepted payload bytes per session — the authoritative document_md bytes accepted at open plus the gross content bytes of every accepted patch, so replace-with-smaller traffic cannot cycle it), STREAM_BUDGET_MAX_SECTIONS = 4096 checked at /stream/open on the post-dedup list produced by build_sections_from_init (patch path needs no section check — sections are fixed at open), and a token bucket of STREAM_BUDGET_RATE_PER_MINUTE = 30 sustained / STREAM_BUDGET_RATE_BURST = 60 refilling one token per 2 seconds, charged only on new in-sync patches actually applied — duplicate retransmits short-circuit free before any budget logic, needs_resync responses stay free (nothing applied), and /stream/heartbeat and /stream/close stay budget-free (the keepalive carries no content). Every exceed is refused with a named BLOCK marker in the file's voice — BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_BYTES_EXCEEDED, BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_SECTIONS_EXCEEDED, BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_RATE_EXCEEDED — a plain status code (413 / 413 / 429) through the existing {"error": ...} JSON body naming the budget and the cap, with NO wire-format change: DocOpenResponse and DocPatchResponse keep their fields, so the renderer event stream (mt::live::update doc_open/doc_patch/doc_close payloads) is byte-compatible. On every refusal the session keeps its last valid revision — revision, last_seq, document_md, sections and the emitted frontend state untouched, session stays active (never killed without notice) — and the bucket decision is extracted as a pure function beside apply_section_patch and decide_open so it is testable without real-time waits. Budget state lives on the LiveSession struct (NOT LiveServerState, so the LiveServerState literal in src-tauri/src/main.rs stays untouched; the only other LiveSession literal — the #[ignore] load smoke at tests.rs:469 — is updated in scope) and is replaced wholesale by a same-session resync re-open (ReplaceSameSession rebuilds the LiveSession literal), keeping the documented resync recovery for a client that hit the cap honestly; per-opens quota abuse is thereby possible and is an explicit NonGoal together with cross-session accounting. The renderer liveViewer bridge has no error branch today and stays untouched — renderer is NOT in scope. live_server.rs is compiled under --features app-store (only the listener start is cfg-gated in main.rs), so the budget code must compile and the m045_ext suite must stay green under the app-store feature — verified by an app-store cargo gate. Governance: exactly ONE new CHANGE_SUMMARY line in the live_server.rs module contract, one M-045 SummaryDelta line, one V-M-045 scenario plus the three new markers; the seven pinned stream_budget tests are red-first (fail against the baseline tree, pass after). Execution mode: T-001..T-003 run strictly sequentially in one module (single-writer discipline), each gated by the m045_ext cargo filter suite; no grace-lint command appears inside this plan — lint runs only in the external target/final phases.

T-001.Title: Session budget state on LiveSession plus the cumulative byte and section-count caps at open/patch with their BLOCK markers

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Budget state is a struct on the session, not on shared server state: a StreamBudget struct (cumulative accepted payload bytes: u64, rate bucket state for T-002 — available tokens: f64 and last_refill: Instant, initialized at burst) is added as the field `pub budget: StreamBudget` on LiveSession (live_server.rs:73), the two named constants land beside it — STREAM_BUDGET_TOTAL_BYTES: u64 = 67108864 (64 MiB, written as the plain literal so the value is greppable) and STREAM_BUDGET_MAX_SECTIONS: usize = 4096 — and every LiveSession construction site builds a fresh StreamBudget: the handle_doc_open literal (:817) covers both FreshOpen and the ReplaceSameSession resync path (wholesale rebuild = budgets reset, the documented recovery for a client that hit the cap honestly), and the only other literal — the #[ignore] load smoke at tests.rs:469 — is updated in the same task; LiveServerState and its struct literals (src-tauri/src/main.rs:799, tests.rs:963) are untouched, so main.rs stays out of the bundle, and Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock are untouched (no new dependency: byte counting is len() on owned strings, elapsed arithmetic uses the already-imported std::time::Instant).

The open path refuses over-budget opens before any session or frontend state exists: after build_sections_from_init produces the post-dedup list, a list longer than STREAM_BUDGET_MAX_SECTIONS is refused with safe_eprintln BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_SECTIONS_EXCEEDED and a 413 (StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE) whose body is the existing {"error": ...} shape naming the budget and the cap (the refusal text carries the 4096 figure); a section list of exactly 4096 passes. The byte cap then checks the authoritative stored document — document_md.len() where document_md is exactly today's value (rebuild_document_md of the sections when sections are non-empty, initial_md otherwise; no protocol change to that choice) — and an initial payload larger than STREAM_BUDGET_TOTAL_BYTES is refused with BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_BYTES_EXCEEDED and 413; an initial payload of exactly 67108864 bytes passes (refusal is strictly "would push past the cap", acceptance invariant is cumulative <= cap). Both refusals happen before the session literal is built, before *session_guard = Some(...) and before emit_doc_open: no session is created, the previous session (in the Conflict/ForeignOwner-checked window) and the frontend event stream are untouched, and DocOpenRequest/DocOpenResponse fields are unchanged.

The patch path refuses patches that would push the cumulative total past the cap, leaving the last valid revision untouched: charged bytes are the GROSS content bytes of every accepted patch (req.content.len() for both append and replace — counting only net growth would be cycle-able by replace-with-smaller traffic, which the spec forbids), checked at the single apply site inside START_BLOCK_APPLY_PATCH (live_server.rs:961) immediately before apply_section_patch; when session.budget.cumulative_bytes + req.content.len() as u64 would exceed STREAM_BUDGET_TOTAL_BYTES the handler logs BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_BYTES_EXCEEDED and returns 413 with the {"error": ...} body naming the budget and the cap, and NOTHING else happens: apply_section_patch is not called, document_md is not rebuilt, last_seq, revision, sections and last_heartbeat are untouched, no mt::live::update is emitted, and the session stays active. On acceptance the cumulative total is advanced by the same gross content bytes before (or atomically with) the apply, then the existing flow (rebuild, last_seq/revision/heartbeat, emit, DocPatchResponse) runs byte-for-byte as today. The duplicate short-circuit (req.seq <= session.last_seq, :920) and the base-revision needs_resync return (:941) keep their exact position BEFORE any budget logic, so duplicates and resync responses are free and byte-checking cannot change their behavior; /stream/heartbeat and /stream/close handlers gain no budget logic; handle_doc_open keeps charging only the authoritative document_md bytes once per (re)open.

The m045_ext filter suite stays green after the task (the pre-existing stream security families exercise open/patch/close/heartbeat paths whose non-budget behavior must not move), and a load-smoke compile check covers the updated tests.rs literal (the test itself remains #[ignore]).

T-002.Title: Token-bucket rate limit: pure decision core beside decide_open plus wiring charged only on applied new-seq patches

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The rate decision is a pure function in the module's existing pure-core style: beside decide_open and apply_section_patch (START_BLOCK_SECTION_PATCH_CORE block), a RateDecision enum (Admit / Exhausted) and `pub fn decide_rate_admission` take the current bucket state (available tokens: f64, last_refill: Instant), the current Instant, and the pinned constants — STREAM_BUDGET_RATE_PER_MINUTE: u32 = 30, STREAM_BUDGET_RATE_BURST: u32 = 60, refill one token per STREAM_BUDGET_REFILL_SECS: u64 = 2 (30/min sustained = 1 per 2 s, burst capacity 60) — computing elapsed = now.duration_since(last_refill), refilling tokens by elapsed/2s capped at the burst, and admitting iff the refilled total is at least 1.0; the function reads no clock itself, touches no session or HTTP state, and returns both the decision and the post-decision bucket state so the caller applies it deterministically — every unit test drives it with synthetic Instants (Instant::now() plus/minus Durations) and never sleeps, keeping the rate family free of real-time waits.

The wiring charges exactly one token per applied patch and nothing else: at the single apply site of START_BLOCK_APPLY_PATCH, after the duplicate short-circuit and the base-revision needs_resync return (both remain free — a needs_resync response applies nothing and is not charged), the handler calls decide_rate_admission with the session's bucket state; on Exhausted it logs BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_RATE_EXCEEDED and returns 429 (StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS) with the {"error": ...} body naming the rate budget and its constants, with zero mutation — the bucket is not debited, last_seq, revision, document_md, sections and last_heartbeat are untouched, no event is emitted, the session stays active, and because last_seq is unchanged a later retransmit of the refused seq is still a new-seq patch that can be admitted once tokens refill; on Admit the handler writes back the debited/refilled bucket state (tokens minus one, last_refill advanced) and proceeds into the unchanged apply flow. The bucket initializes at the burst (60.0 tokens, last_refill = now) inside the fresh StreamBudget built at every (re)open, so a resync re-open resets the rate budget together with the byte budget (per-opens quota abuse is the documented NonGoal). /stream/heartbeat and /stream/close consume nothing and are byte-identical to today.

Boundary semantics are exact: a patch at the bucket boundary (exactly 1.0 token available, no refill time) is ADMITTED and debits to 0.0; a patch with less than 1.0 token (with last_refill close enough to now that no token has accrued) is refused; a duplicate retransmit after exhaustion returns duplicate:true OK and leaves the bucket unchanged; sustained traffic at or below one patch per 2 seconds never refuses regardless of volume. The m045_ext filter suite stays green and the T-001 byte/section behavior is unchanged by this task.

T-003.Title: Red-first stream_budget test family (seven pinned names) plus graph M-045 / verification V-M-045 deltas and the module-contract line

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: tests.rs gains a new paired unique block START_BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_TESTS / END_BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_TESTS inside the existing incoming-data test region, built on the existing stream-fixture harness (incoming_fixture_caps(true, "stream.document") plus direct super::live_server::handle_doc_open / handle_doc_patch / handle_heartbeat calls and f.state.session / f.live_events inspection), carrying exactly the seven pinned async test names: stream_budget_open_refuses_over_total_bytes (an open whose authoritative document exceeds 67108864 bytes yields 413 with the budget named in the error body, state.session stays None, zero live_events); stream_budget_open_refuses_over_section_count (4097 sections yields 413 with the error naming the 4096 cap, no session created); stream_budget_patch_refuses_over_cumulative_bytes (an accepted open followed by a patch that would push the cumulative total past the cap yields 413, and revision, last_seq, document_md and sections are unchanged with zero new events); stream_budget_patch_refuses_over_rate (the session bucket is drained to below one token with last_refill set to now via the fixture's session mutex — no real-time waits — then a new-seq patch yields 429 with revision, last_seq and document unchanged, and an immediate duplicate retransmit of the same seq still returns duplicate:true OK free); stream_budget_rejection_keeps_last_valid_revision (after a byte-class and a rate-class refusal the heartbeat still reports the previous revision, the session is still active, and the next valid in-budget patch on the same base_revision applies normally with needs_resync:false); stream_budget_boundaries_at_exact_cap_pass (an open whose document is exactly 67108864 bytes succeeds, an open with exactly 4096 sections succeeds, a patch landing the cumulative total exactly at the cap succeeds, and a patch at exactly 1.0 bucket token is admitted); stream_budget_under_budget_traffic_unchanged (a normal open → patch → duplicate → heartbeat → close session reproduces today's exact status codes, revision increments 1→2, duplicate:true, heartbeat revision and the doc_open/doc_patch/doc_close event sequence). Assertions are written against the SPEC (413/413/429, the named markers' budgets and caps), never derived from a particular implementation wording.

Red-first evidence is real, not asserted: before recording the green run, the seven tests are executed once against the unchanged baseline tree (a temporary read-only worktree of the change's base commit, or an equivalently exact pre-fix run recorded before T-001/T-002 land) and the all-red outcome — over-cap opens succeed and create sessions, over-rate patches apply — is recorded in the change bundle as the failure evidence; the same family then runs green on the completed tree and the pre-existing m045_ext suite (including the C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH/-TABS/-SCOPE and C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING families) stays green — no existing test body is edited.

Governance deltas land in the same task: live_server.rs gets exactly ONE new CHANGE_SUMMARY line in the START_MODULE_CONTRACT (2026-11-21 C-STREAM-BUDGET: the three per-session budgets, the three BLOCK markers, the 413/413/429 refusals through the existing error shape, last-valid-revision preservation, resync-reopen resets, heartbeat/close free) — every existing CHANGE_SUMMARY line stays byte-identical; .grace/graph/features.xml M-045 gains one appended SummaryDelta line recording the now-true guarantees (touched only inside the M-045 entry, no other module's entry); .grace/verification/features.xml V-M-045 gains one scenario naming the seven pinned stream_budget tests and their red-first status plus three Markers (BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_BYTES_EXCEEDED, BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_SECTIONS_EXCEEDED, BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_RATE_EXCEEDED). The renderer (renderer/liveViewer/index.vue and any store/event code) is touched NOWHERE — it has no error branch and stays untouched by design; wire format and the /ext/* data routes are unchanged; no version bump, no release, no tag.

The app-store cfg alignment gate holds: live_server.rs is compiled under --features app-store (only the listener START is cfg-gated in main.rs), so the completed module compiles and the m045_ext suite passes under --no-default-features --features app-store; any pre-existing app-store failure demonstrably unrelated to this change is recorded in the bundle evidence rather than silently skipped, and the budget code introduces no new cfg arms of its own.

Verification.Command: cargo test --locked --offline --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --no-default-features --features app-store --bin mark m045_ext

AcceptanceVerification.Criterion: Over-budget opens are refused with the explicit budget error and create no session (spec AC-1): stream_budget_open_refuses_over_total_bytes and stream_budget_open_refuses_over_section_count pin the 413 refusals with the cap named in the error, no session in state.session and zero events; the exact-cap boundary CAUTION is pinned by stream_budget_boundaries_at_exact_cap_pass — an open at exactly 67108864 bytes and an open with exactly 4096 post-dedup sections both succeed (acceptance invariant cumulative <= cap; refusal strictly past it).

A patch that would push the cumulative accepted payload bytes past 64 MiB is refused and the last valid revision survives (spec AC-2): stream_budget_patch_refuses_over_cumulative_bytes pins the 413 with revision, last_seq, document_md, sections and the event stream untouched; stream_budget_rejection_keeps_last_valid_revision pins that the heartbeat still reports the previous revision, the session is still active, and the next valid in-budget patch on the same base_revision applies normally with needs_resync:false — the session is never killed, reset or resync-forced by a refusal.

An exhausted rate bucket refuses the patch with state untouched and the boundary admits (spec AC-3): stream_budget_patch_refuses_over_rate pins the 429 with revision, last_seq and document unchanged, duplicate retransmits consuming nothing (their short-circuit at live_server.rs:920 stays before all budget logic), heartbeat and close staying budget-free, and the pure decide_rate_admission core pins the boundary (exactly 1.0 token admits; one token per 2 s refill; 60 burst) without real-time waits.

Under-budget traffic behaves exactly as before (spec AC-4): stream_budget_under_budget_traffic_unchanged reproduces the pre-change status codes, revision increments, duplicate and resync semantics, heartbeat responses and the emitted mt::live::update sequence on a normal patch session; the pre-existing stream security families stay green and unedited.

Resync-reopen resets budgets and this is the honest client's documented recovery: the ReplaceSameSession wholesale rebuild builds a fresh StreamBudget, so a client that hit the cap can re-open with the same session_id and continue; cross-session quotas and persistence beyond the live session are explicit NonGoals (per-opens quota abuse is accepted and documented in the module contract line), pinned by the resync-reset behavior in the boundary/rejection tests.

Renderer and wire format are provably untouched: the renderer has no error branch and is not in ObservedWriteScope (expected diff: none); DocOpenRequest/DocOpenResponse/DocPatchRequest/DocPatchResponse fields are unchanged, refusals ride plain 413/413/429 through the existing {"error": ...} body, and the mt::live::update event payloads stay byte-compatible — nothing in the bundle touches liveViewer, the store, or /ext/* data routes.

Governance and gates: the seven pinned stream_budget tests are red against the baseline tree and green after (recorded red evidence in the bundle); the m045_ext cargo filter is green on the default build AND under --no-default-features --features app-store (budget code is cfg-neutral; any pre-existing app-store failure is recorded, not hidden); the graph and verification XML parse; exactly one new CHANGE_SUMMARY line exists in the live_server.rs module contract with all prior lines byte-identical; one M-045 SummaryDelta and one V-M-045 scenario plus three markers land; no version bump, no release publication; grace lint runs only in the external target/final phases — this plan contains no self-referential grace-lint MustPassCommand.
